title: Google Genie 3 Can Generate Playable Worlds From a Prompt
author: No-Blackberry-7564

comments.author: Competitive_Ad_9995
comments.body:
0:40 we can see a tree between 2 houses. Camera moves few angles away, return in few seconds and one house lost. There are one house and tree. There are much more problems like this, but this is biggest one because in video were focus on small street on other side of lost house.

This Genie 3 can't hold in memory even few seconds out of view for few angles, just remember very light context and trying to regenerate. 

Cool for short video or for research tasks, but it's even not close to anything playable in any visible feature. Maximum - infinite railroad run games like Minion Rush or Subway Surf where you will never rotate your camera but you will get infinite generated road. 

And it's even if not to remember that there are only movement and jump, 0 other mechanics.

comments.author: ScrapyJack
comments.body:
Without temporal consistency it's not a game, it's an interactive art piece. Without a consistent or predictable world there is nothing here but a strange novelty. If it could be bound to a pre-established geomancy and work like a filter I bet you could do something awesome. As it is now, kinda worthless.

I'll check back up on this in a few years.

replies.author: No-Blackberry-7564
replies.body:
that's a fair criticism. temporal consistency is one of the biggest hurdles for these world models right now.
that said, a lot of new technologies look like novelties before the core problems get solved. If future versions can maintain a stable world state or operate on predefined geometry like you mentioned, the use cases become much more interesting. for now, it's more of a glimpse at what's possible than a replacement for actual games

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body:
I don't think video gen based "world model" maximalism is anything other than a dead end. We're already at a point where advanced video models are not really sustainable at a customer level, and this is just using that technology and overextending it *even further*. The way they're doing this is basically just brute-forcing the most expensive technology they have instead of building something with some persistence and actual constraints.

Something like this cannot be video gen based. The better way to make something like this happen is by building the actual models & maps rapidly and accurately. But that's actually much harder than repeatedly bashing a stadium full of servers against the problem until it goes away.

replies.author: No-Blackberry-7564
replies.body: You might be right about the long term limitations but people said similar things about early image and video models. Sometimes the first generation is inefficient and the real breakthroughs come from optimizing what initially looked impractical
